c1-05.title: Fixing up the house
c1-05.story: On Saturday, Anna's family decided to fix up the house before the grandparents arrived. Dad spent the morning painting the hallway, starting with a coat of [[primer]] so the old stains wouldn't show through. Mama replaced the broken soap [[dispenser]] in the bathroom, while Taras cleaned the [[aquarium]] and talked to the fish the whole time. The front door lock kept sticking, so Max came over and took its [[mechanism]] apart on the kitchen table. Meanwhile, Anna found her old [[scrapbook]] and used a strong [[adhesive]] to reattach the photos that had fallen out. When Grandma and Grandpa arrived, Grandpa proudly held up a [[carp]] he had caught in the lake that morning. Grandma had brought a gift too: a hand-made [[quilt]] for Taras's bed. Taras stared at the fish, then at his tank, and asked if it could live with him. Everyone laughed, and the fish went to the kitchen instead.

c1-06.title: Buying winter clothes
c1-06.story: When the first snow fell in Kyiv, Anna realized her old coat wouldn't survive another winter. She and Lisa spent Saturday at the mall, trying on everything from [[flannel]] shirts to a stiff [[tweed]] jacket that made Lisa look like a professor. Anna fell in love with a soft [[cashmere]] scarf, but the price tag made her put it back. In a vintage shop, Lisa tried on a lace [[corset]] just for fun and couldn't stop laughing at herself in the mirror. Anna finally chose a warm wool [[cape]] that was surprisingly cheap. At the register, the cashier mentioned that the store offered a small [[rebate]] if she filled out a form online. That evening, Anna listed her old coat on an online [[marketplace]], and someone bought it within an hour. With the extra money, she went back the next day and bought the scarf after all.

c1-07.title: At the jeweler's
c1-07.story: Max wanted to buy something special for his mother's birthday, so he asked Anna to come with him. The first store they visited was so [[high-end]] that a single ring cost more than Max's whole summer job had paid. They moved on to a small family jeweler's, where the owner showed them a tray of stones. Anna liked a deep purple [[amethyst]], while Max kept going back to a milky [[opal]] that flashed with color in the light. The owner explained that the price depended on each stone's [[carat]] weight, not just its color. Max also looked at watches, but he decided a simple [[quartz]] model wasn't personal enough. In the end, he chose a silver [[medallion]] with the opal set in the middle. The owner placed it in a small box lined with silk dyed with [[indigo]]. His mother cried when she opened it, and Max pretended he had chosen it all by himself.

c1-08.title: Looking after yourself
c1-08.story: Anna's mama won a free day at a [[wellness]] center, and she invited Anna and Sofia to come along. They started in the [[sauna]], where Sofia lasted only five minutes before running out for cold water. At lunch, the menu was all salmon and seeds, and a waiter proudly explained how much [[omega-3]] each dish contained. In the afternoon, Mama tried a facial with an [[anti-aging]] cream that smelled like roses, while Anna got her first [[manicure]]. Sofia went to the salon for [[styling]] and asked the stylist to shape her curls into a big, round [[afro]]. She looked amazing and couldn't stop taking selfies. On the way home, Sofia suddenly realized she had left her [[retainer]] on the lunch table. They drove all the way back, and the waiter handed it to her, wrapped in a napkin, with a smile.

c1-09.title: A day at the hospital
c1-09.story: Anna went with her grandfather to the hospital for his yearly heart checkup. At the [[front office]], a nurse checked his name and reminded him that his [[pacemaker]] would also be tested. While they waited, a man was rushed in with [[hypothermia]] after falling through the ice while fishing. A girl with minor head [[trauma]] from a bike accident sat next to them, and Grandpa kept her laughing with his old stories. Later, the doctor asked about every [[risk factor]], from his diet to the pipe he still smoked on weekends. Then she sent him for a [[stress test]] on a treadmill, which he complained about the whole time. An eye specialist also examined his [[retina]], because his vision had been getting blurry. Since he was slightly dehydrated, the doctor suggested a drink to replace his lost [[electrolytes|electrolyte]]. Grandpa joked that with his new tooth [[implant]] and all his heart equipment, he was already half machine. On the way out, he promised Anna he would finally give up the pipe.

c1-10.title: Expecting a baby
c1-10.story: Max's aunt was in her second [[trimester]], and Sofia couldn't stop asking her questions about the baby. One afternoon, Sofia and Anna went with her to a routine appointment. The doctor did an ultrasound [[screening]] and showed them the baby's tiny hands on the screen. She explained that the [[placenta]] was healthy and in the right place, which was good news. When the aunt complained that she was always hungry, the doctor laughed and said pregnancy speeds up your [[metabolism]]. The aunt also blamed a certain [[hormone]] for making her cry at TV commercials. Before they left, the nurse gave her a [[booster]] shot to protect both her and the baby. On the bus home, Sofia announced that she was going to become a doctor, at least until next week.

c1-11.title: Talking about mental health
c1-11.story: Anna's school held a mental health week, and Anna and Ira volunteered to make posters for the hallway. Their teacher said the goal was to break the [[stigma]] that stops students from asking for help. Ira admitted that in her family, talking about feelings had always been a bit of a [[taboo]]. One poster explained that [[self-harm]] is a sign that someone is in pain and needs support, not judgment. Another listed a free helpline for anyone in [[distress]], day or night. On Wednesday, the school counselor ran a [[stress management]] workshop before exams, and every seat was taken. A guest speaker described her [[coming out]] as a teenager and how much her friends' support had meant to her. Max hung a poster saying that [[hate speech]] has no place in the school, online or offline. Ira flipped through a pile of [[self-help]] books in the library but decided a walk with friends worked better for her. By Friday, Anna noticed a real change in [[mindset]]: students were actually asking each other how they felt.

c1-12.title: Sex education class
c1-12.story: Anna's biology class began its sex education unit, and a few students giggled nervously at the first slide. The teacher calmly explained the female reproductive system, including the [[vagina]] and the uterus, with a simple diagram. She then covered infections such as [[herpes]], which causes painful sores, and [[syphilis]], which can be cured with antibiotics if caught early. When a boy asked about [[porno]], she said it gives a false picture of real relationships and of consent. She added that [[libido]] is simply sexual desire and that it naturally changes with stress, sleep, and age. The textbook also noted that an [[orgasm]] releases hormones that help the body relax, which made Max turn bright red. Just then, a loud rumbling filled the room, because workers outside were using a concrete [[vibrator]] on the new school steps. Everyone burst out laughing, and the teacher had to wait until the noise stopped. In history class afterward, Ira presented a carved wooden [[fetish]], a holy object from an old religion, borrowed from the city museum. Anna decided it had been a very educational day in more ways than one.
